what_was_done: The allow-list does not follow the grammar it states. caller.py line 91 is _QUOTED = r"'[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]*'". It excludes control characters and DEL but not the single quote, although the comment beside it says 'no quote' and rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md says 'A single-quoted string holds no single quote'. So an argument that starts and ends with a single quote may hold every excluded character in between. 'vsdd survey 'x'; id; 'y'' and 'vsdd survey ''$(id)''' both match _CALL_TEXT_RE. Only the parser refuses them, the first by its segment count and the second by its opacity. 'vsdd survey 'a'b'' passes both gates. For any text between an outer pair of quotes, approval again rests on the parser alone, which is the deny-list ORCH-2 set out to stop relying on. No test catches this. The tests check is_vsdd_call(parse(text)), so the parser hides any hole in the regex. The property test leaves the single quote out of its alphabet and never puts junk between quotes. Everything else ORCH-2 asked for is in place, and stripping the allow-list in a scratch copy fails three tests. To fix it: write _QUOTED = r"'[^'\x00-\x1f\x7f]*'". In a scratch copy that change keeps the 75 tests in test_caller.py, test_shell.py and test_runner.py passing. Then assert caller._CALL_TEXT_RE.fullmatch(text) is None, on the regex alone, for every REFUSED_CALLS and LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS entry. Add 'vsdd survey 'a'b'', 'vsdd survey 'a''b'', 'vsdd survey 'x'; id; 'y'' and 'vsdd survey ''$(id)'''. Give the property test a fourth position that puts junk, drawn from the excluded characters plus the single quote, between two quotes.
